criteria.statement: Improved sparse-autoencoder reconstruction does not establish usefulness, research value, or external utility.
Interpretability should improve a hard external outcome stated without interpretability jargon, such as finding adversarial examples faster than prior techniques.
A valid external target is detecting verifiably false model statements more often than comparison methods.
Choose outcomes that are difficult to game or self-deceive about, so correct insights create measurable progress.
Progress toward truth is not automatically progress toward AI safety; tasks should be AGI-relevant proxies.
Test nontrivial explanations of confusing actions and predictions of prompt changes that alter behavior.
Evidence should help distinguish scheming from confusion or instruction misunderstanding.
Full reverse engineering and deep confidence are likely unrealistic given model complexity and flawed human ontologies.
Use whatever works, including non-internals methods, and select tasks where interpretability has comparative advantage.
Solve important proxy tasks directly even when interpretability is irrelevant, such as preventing models from lying to users.
Preserve scientific decomposition, mechanism understanding, and principle-finding even when interpretability is not the right tool.
Safety research should include more methods that actually align models rather than only papering over failures with adjacent work.
Complex agent-produced technical work requires debugging for mistakes and security flaws; autonomous output alone is insufficient.
Qualitative capability or scale transitions can invalidate technique assumptions, and adaptation may or may not work.
Highly zoomed-in neuron-and-head circuit methods are less likely to scale because they depend heavily on current architectures.
Many concepts are represented as linear directions accessible to probes and steering, with nonlinear probes as a fallback.
Reading chain of thought is currently effective monitoring because present models struggle to act sneakily without verbalizing reasoning.
Chain-of-thought monitoring is unlikely to remain effective through superintelligence.
Chain-of-thought monitoring can fail through evaluation awareness, greater within-forward-pass reasoning, or vector-based reasoning traces.
Text chain of thought currently increases available sequential reasoning beyond one forward pass.
Important concepts such as deception may remain human-comprehensible, while alien concepts are likelier in vastly superhuman domains.
Interpretability agents are useful and likely necessary because evidence volume exceeds human review capacity.
Test agent trustworthiness and collusion, and whether prior-generation models or tools can comprehend newer models.
Character or constitutional training may generalize alignment across contexts better than ordinary post-training.
Broad alignment generalization cannot rest on one contrived role-playing OOD evaluation; test diverse settings instead of assuming success.

Because alignment is fundamentally generalization, tests must cover OOD behavior, training awareness, and alignment faking rather than narrow training performance.

Activation probes are cheap and fairly effective cyber-misuse monitors.
Extend probes to detect whether a model takes actions it knows would be disapproved.
Coding-agent evaluations should cover unauthorized deletion, corner-cutting, lying, exaggerated completion claims, data destruction, and poor clarification calibration.
Favor safety work with immediate product relevance because cheap deployment materially improves adoption odds.
Interpretability currently has little post-training feedback loop; a stronger impact path is misalignment auditing or deeper alignment-relevant understanding.
Compare post-training interventions using strong evaluations that explicitly measure whether alignment generalizes.
A persuasive intervention materially improves agent-safety evaluations while capability evaluations remain equal or improve slightly.
Evidence burden should rise with intervention complexity, and large pipeline changes require strong evidence and stakeholder-relevant framing.
Projects should identify their theory of change, such as public field influence, reusable open source, or direct internal deployment.
Sparse-autoencoder post-training may yield small gains, but most ideas fail at frontier scale and meaningful production impact remains unobserved at DeepMind.
Improving current-model safety usually also increases capability, usefulness, and lab revenue, making dual use difficult to avoid.
Good empirical safety research needs rich feedback from real models; isolation from production systems weakens research.
Repeated small safety deployments build trust, infrastructure knowledge, and capacity to deliver larger future interventions.
Interpretability insights such as superposition may create capability externalities through better architecture design.
